property_summary: P.supportsInterface should return true for the IAccessControl interfaceId and false for other interfaceIds, but M.supportsInterface returns true for any interfaceId including ones that are not IAccessControl.

For any valid bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId (as inherited from AccessControl and ERC165), but the mutant always returns false, breaking the required interface support check.

For any bytes4 interfaceId that is either type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true in the reference, but the mutant returns false for such interfaceIds.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true if and only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for those interfaceIds, violating the rule.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface should return true for IAccessControl and IERC165, but the mutant returns false, violating ERC165 compliance.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return false only if interfaceId is not supported; the mutant returns false for all interfaceIds, including those that must be supported (e.g., type(IERC165).interfaceId or type(IAccessControl).interfaceId).

The reference contract correctly returns true for supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId), whereas the mutant incorrectly returns false because it delegates solely to ERC165 which only recognizes the IERC165 interface.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, then supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false because it only delegates to ERC165.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false because it only delegates to ERC165.
supportsInterface must return true for any interfaceId that the contract claims to support via its inheritance; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.
For any account and role, if the account has been granted that role via _grantRole, hasRole must return true; the mutant always returns false, so it will return false even for newly granted roles.

For any role and account, hasRole must equal the actual membership in _roles. The mutant always returns false, so after _setupRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, someone) in the constructor, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, that address) will differ.

For any role and any account that has been assigned the role by having the contract grant itself that role via the public grantRole entrypoint (which it can as admin of itself), hasRole must return true; the mutant always returns false, violating this.

For any role R and account A that has been granted R after deployment via the public grantRole entry point by an admin, hasRole(R, A) must return true in the reference contract; the mutant always returns false, breaking this property.

For any role that is open (i.e., the open-role address(0) member is set to true) and any account that has been granted that role, calling hasRole from that account during execution of a function guarded by onlyRoleOrOpenRole must succeed without reverting; the mutant's hasRole always returns false, causing a revert where the reference allows the call.
For any role and account, the result of hasRole must equal the internal membership mapping; the mutant negates the membership so it returns true exactly when the account does NOT have the role.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) returns the same boolean as (c.getRoleAdmin(role) == c.getRoleAdmin(role)), which must hold true by reflexivity; the bug negates the membership check so for a non-member the reference returns the contradictory value.
For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) returns true if and only if the account has the role; the mutant negates the membership check so the result is inverted.

For any role and account, calling hasRole(role, account) twice in a row must return the same boolean value; the bug negates the internal flag so a correctly initialized role will change its result after revocation.
For any role and account, the result of hasRole(role, account) must equal the result of _roles[role].members[account], but the bug negates the membership so the two always differ.
After a call to renounceRole, the caller must not lose the role unless they are the account being renounced, but the bug allows any caller to revoke any account's role.

A non-self caller can renounce another account's role in the buggy version, causing the role to be revoked for that account, whereas in the reference version the require(account == msg.sender) prevents this.

After any call to renounceRole, the caller's own membership status for the given role must remain unchanged, but the bug allows any caller to revoke the role from a different account while the caller itself still holds the role.
